journal_lines: Old logging camp. Whoever left it behind didn't come back. We did the math.
Abandoned camp in the timber. Tools still there. Took what was useful.
Woodcutter's camp. Long since empty. The iron and the logs were still worth having.
Found the camp where the big trees were felled. No one around. Helped ourselves.
A coat on a peg, weather-rotted. A bowl on the table, full of leaves now. Took the iron, left the rest.
Stumps the size of cartwheels, all around the clearing. Whoever had worked here had worked.
Camp tools laid out as if for the morning. The morning had not come for years.
Picked through the camp slowly, respectfully. They had not chosen to leave it. Maybe.
